meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это не воровство, послушай! Это абсолютно безопасно.
examples.trans: That's not stealing, listen! It's completely safe.

meanings.note: At an office, hotel, or cemetery. Borrowed from Latin agent/instrument noun in '-tor' ('администратор'). Common masculine noun meaning 'administrator, manager, receptionist' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Входишь сразу налево, к администратору. Там сидит такой Лисицын.
examples.trans: You go in and turn straight left, to the administrator. A fellow named Lisitsyn sits there.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'бояться собак'. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be afraid (of), to fear'.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'together' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы с Пашей вместе уже месяц.
examples.trans: Pasha and I have been together for a month now.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'near, beside, right by' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm listening right by my ear.
The car is parked near the house.

examples.text: Возле дома Аникеева ходили два подозрительных человека.

meanings.note: важный вопрос = an important matter
важный вопрос = an important matter

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

выходить.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to come out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.
Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выйти'.

examples.trans: I'm going out in a minute.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('stupid, silly, foolish').

examples.text: Ваня, ты глупый? Зачем ты сейчас это при нём сказал?

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

ехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride

meanings.en: to go, to drive, to ride
meanings.note: by car, bus, train, in one direction, now
'едем' = we're going / let's go. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to drive, to ride', paired with 'поехать'.

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!

Damage something or ruin relations. Prefix 'ис-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'портить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to spoil, ruin, damage', paired with 'портить'.

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

находиться.gloss: to be located, to be found

meanings.en: to be located, to be situated
meanings.note: Imperfective reflexive verb. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'ходиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be located, to be found', paired with 'найтись'.

examples.trans: Where is the operating room located?

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
